claims.text: The onset of melting in FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by selective Cu segregation to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface Cu enrichment creates a region with a lower local melting point.
The Cu-enriched surface triggers formation of a liquid-like surface layer.
The liquid-like surface layer progresses toward complete melting as temperature increases.
The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are compositionally homogeneous.
Sub-premelting pre-annealing homogenizes the nanoparticle composition and inhibits Cu segregation.
As-prepared control nanoparticles retain a native Cu-rich surface.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other alloying elements in FeNiCrCoCu.
Cu preferentially segregates to the surface of unmodified FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu surface segregation reduces local thermal stability and initiates surface liquefaction below the bulk melting temperature.
Composition homogenization by pre-annealing prevents Cu segregation and delays premelting onset.
Pre-annealed nanoparticles will have a higher surface-melting onset temperature than untreated nanoparticles.
Pre-annealing will measurably alter the extent and rate of liquid-layer progression during premelting.
Untreated FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles naturally develop a Cu-rich surface and exhibit earlier premelting.
The premelting-onset shift caused by suppressing Cu segregation depends on particle size and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial particles are described as compositionally homogeneous, while the as-prepared untreated particles are also described as retaining or naturally possessing a native Cu-rich surface. The hypothesis does not clarify whether 'homogeneous' excludes the surface, or whether Cu enrichment develops only during subsequent heating.
